overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic late-June marine layer day with patchy fog, mostly cloudy skies, and a mild onshore southwest flow keeping temperatures suppressed. As of 12:09 ET (9:09 AM PDT), the running max is 66.2°F — still warming at +1.8°F/hr with several hours remaining before the afternoon peak. The active regional alerts (Extreme Heat Warnings, Red Flag Warnings, Air Quality Alerts) are all confined to inland desert and mountain zones well away from coastal LA and have no direct bearing on today's coastal forecast.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are reasonably well-clustered — ECMWF at 68.4°F, NBM at 67.0°F, and the NWS official forecast at 69°F are in close agreement, while HRRR is a modest warm outlier at 71.1°F. Current observations are tracking near the lower end of the forecast envelope given the marine layer, but the predicted peak timing of 16–17h ET (1–2 PM PDT) means meaningful additional warming is expected before the day's high is set.
max_temp_prediction: The META model — the most reliable fused signal — places a dominant 47.5% probability on the 70–71°F bucket, with secondary support for 66–67°F (26.5%), yielding a probability-weighted expected value near 70°F. The NWS official forecast of 69°F and the ECMWF/NBM consensus around 67–68°F collectively anchor the distribution in the upper 60s to low 70s. Given the current running max of 66.2°F, continued onshore flow, and partial cloud cover limiting solar heating, confidence is moderate-high for a final TMAX in the 69–71°F range, with 70°F as the single best estimate.
